notes: Arduino MKR Zero was not in the catalogue and lookup_part found nothing, so a new part type 'arduino-mkr-zero' was drafted (MKR pin layout plus BAT, SD and USB sockets).
The text says to plug the MKR Zero into the breadboard, but the circuit image shows it beside the breadboard, connected by three jumper wires. I followed the image.

The DHT22 (labelled RHT03 in the image) sits in row a of columns 25-28 in pin order VCC, SDA (data), NC, GND. The red wire is in column 25 (VCC to MKR VCC, 3.3 V), the orange wire in column 26 (data to D7), and the black wire in column 28 (GND to MKR GND). Column 27 (NC) is unused.
The 100nF capacitor goes between column 25 (power) and column 28 (GND). The 4.7k pull-up resistor goes between column 25 (power) and column 26 (data). Exact rows b, d and e are read from the image.
The DHT22 is powered from the 3.3 V VCC pin, which is within its 3.3-6 V range.

The microSD card goes in the MKR Zero's built-in slot. The LiPo battery plugs into the MKR Zero's JST BAT connector, so its leads are not wired to individual ports. The USB cable used for programming is not in the parts list, so it is not modelled.
The resistor value is 4.7k (the parts list says 4.75k, the text says 4k7). No electrical edge is added for the DHT22's NC pin.
